City council approves the harbour rebuild

The city council voted on Tuesday evening to approve the harbour rebuild, ending a debate that had run for most of three years and had twice been postponed after residents objected to the cost estimates attached to the earlier drafts.

Under the approved plan the eastern quay will be rebuilt first, followed by the ferry terminal and the two access roads that carry freight traffic away from the residential streets on the northern side of the basin.

The council's own estimate puts the total cost at just under two hundred million, spread across eleven years. An independent review commissioned by the opposition put the figure roughly fifteen per cent higher, largely because it assumed a slower schedule for the dredging work.

Councillor Reyes, who chaired the planning committee, said the vote settled the question of whether the rebuild would happen at all, and that the remaining disagreements were about sequencing rather than principle.

Opponents said the approval had come before the traffic study was published. The council replied that the study would be released in the autumn and that the first contracts would not be signed until it had been considered.

Work on the eastern quay is expected to begin next spring, once the seasonal restrictions on dredging have lifted and the harbour authority has completed the survey of the existing piles.
